mainTopic: The amounts of oil in the משנה: half a לוג for the תודה, one לוג per מנחה or per עשרון, the נסכים measured in הין and לוג, and half a לוג per lamp of the מנורה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier point: even the mouths of the מנורה's lamps must be made of pure gold. The גמרא then works through the oil amounts listed in the משנה. For the תודה, רבי עקיבא learns half a לוג from the double ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״, read as a ריבוי אחר ריבוי that comes to limit. Half of that oil goes to the רביכה. רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says the half לוג is instead a הלכה למשה מסיני. Next, the חכמים hold that each עשרון of flour needs one לוג of oil, while רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב say every מנחה gets only one לוג. Each side explains how it uses the other side's words in the poor מצורע's פסוק. The גמרא then gives the sources for the נסכים amounts, using the fact that a הין is twelve לוגין, and for the half לוג per lamp of the מנורה, which the חכמים measured to last all night. The amud ends with the start of a new משנה about which נסכים may be mixed together.

steps.title: Why the teaching about pure gold is needed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its earlier answer: without the ברייתא, we might have thought the mouths of the מנורה's lamps could be made of any kind of gold, so the ברייתא tells us they must be pure gold.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you might have said: let it be made from gold of any quality. That is why the ברייתא needs to teach us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes a discussion from the previous page. It explains why the ברייתא had to spell out that the lamps' mouths are made of pure gold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier question was why the ברייתא needed to say this at all. The answer is that we might have thought any gold is fine for this part of the מנורה. The phrase קא משמע לן means the ברייתא is coming to block that wrong idea.

keyTerms.meaning: And let it be made (a suggestion of what we might have thought)
Gold of any quality, not necessarily pure
It teaches us. This is the reason a source had to state something

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא's wording is needed: even the mouths of the lamps of the מנורה must be made of pure gold.

phrases.english: and let it be made from gold of any quality,
phrases.notes: This is still about the mouths of the מנורה's lamps from the discussion just before this.

phrases.english: so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלֶיעְבֵּד זָהָב כֹּל דְּהוּ, קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from the previous page about why the ברייתא mentions pure gold for the lamps' mouths.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains why a seemingly unneeded statement is necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The mouths of the lamps could be made of gold of any quality.
steps.terutzMaskana: They must be made of pure gold, as the ברייתא teaches.

steps.title: The משנה: half a לוג of oil for the thanks offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: the תודה loaves use half a לוג of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: Half a לוג of oil for the thanks offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic by quoting the משנה's rule that the תודה uses half a לוג of oil. This sets up the next step, where a source for this amount is brought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Most מנחות use a full לוג of oil. The תודה is different and uses only half a לוג. That difference is what needs a source.

keyTerms.meaning: Half a לוג, a liquid measure
Thanks offering, brought together with four kinds of loaves
Oil

phrases.english: A half-log of oil for the thanks offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves away from the מנורה discussion to a new line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The loaves of the תודה use half a לוג of oil.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא learns half a לוג from the double ״בשמן״
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא explains that the double ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ is a ריבוי אחר ריבוי, and such a double amplification comes to limit. So the oil is reduced from one לוג to half a לוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי עקיבא says: Why does the פסוק say ״with oil״ twice? If it had said ״with oil״ only once, I would have said the תודה is like all other מנחות, which need one לוג. Now that it wrote ״with oil״ twice, that is an amplification after an amplification. An amplification after an amplification only comes to limit. So the פסוק limited it to half a לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא brings רבי עקיבא's source for the משנה's half a לוג. He reads the word ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״, which the פסוק writes twice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With just one ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״, the תודה would follow the normal rule of one לוג like every other מנחה. The second ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ creates a ריבוי אחר ריבוי. By רבי עקיבא's rule, two inclusive words in a row actually reduce the amount, so here it drops to half a לוג.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this? It asks why a word is there
I would have said. This is the mistaken idea we might have had
Meal offerings, which normally need one לוג of oil
An amplification after an amplification: two inclusive words in a row
Only to limit or reduce

steps.confusionAlert: It sounds backwards, but here two inclusive words do not add more. By this rule, a ריבוי אחר ריבוי comes to reduce the amount.

phrases.english: It is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Akiva says:
Why must the verse state
"with oil," "with oil," two times?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12

phrases.english: Had only one "with oil" been stated,
I would have said:
it is like all the meal offerings, needing a log.
Now that it wrote "with oil," "with oil,"
it is an amplification after an amplification,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין רִיבּוּי אַחַר רִיבּוּי אֶלָּא לְמַעֵט –
phrases.english: and an amplification after an amplification serves only to limit —
the verse limited it to a half-log.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא: רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא אוֹמֵר: מָה תַּלְמוּד לוֹמַר ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ שְׁנֵי פְּעָמִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק source for the משנה's half a לוג.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The double ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ is a ריבוי אחר ריבוי, which comes to limit, so the תודה uses half a לוג instead of a full לוג.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets out רבי עקיבא's reading method: two inclusive words in a row reduce the amount. The next step tests whether this case really fits that rule.

steps.title: Challenge: there is only one amplification here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions רבי עקיבא's reading. The first ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ seems needed just to require oil at all, so only the second one is an amplification.
steps.simpleTranslation: An amplification after an amplification?! It is only one amplification!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא. It argues that there aren't really two amplifications, only one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the ברייתא's own words, one ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ would have taught that the תודה needs oil like other מנחות, so that word is used for a basic rule. That leaves only the second ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ as extra. Without two extra words, the rule of ריבוי אחר ריבוי seems not to apply here.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only one amplification
One (Aramaic)

phrases.english: An amplification after an amplification?!
It is only one amplification!
phrases.notes: He means the first ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ is already used to teach that oil is needed, so only the second one is extra.

steps.triggerLanguage: רִיבּוּי אַחַר רִיבּוּי?! חַד רִיבּוּי הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reasoning of רבי עקיבא's derivation in step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי עקיבא's claim that the double ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ is a ריבוי אחר ריבוי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ is needed for the basic oil requirement, so it is not an amplification. That leaves only one amplification, and one amplification cannot trigger the limiting rule.

steps.title: Rewording רבי עקיבא so both ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ are amplifications
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rewords רבי עקיבא's statement. Without any ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״, the תודה loaves would get a full לוג like all מנחות. So both mentions are extra, and the double ריבוי cuts the amount to half a לוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, read it like this: if the פסוק had not said ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ at all, I would have said the תודה is like all other מנחות and gets a לוג of oil. Now that it says ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״, that is one ריבוי after another. A ריבוי after a ריבוי only comes to limit, so the פסוק limited it to half a לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its own question from Step 4 by fixing how רבי עקיבא's words should be read.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 asked whether the first ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ was needed just to require oil at all. The answer is no: even with no ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״, the תודה would already get oil, a full לוג like every other מנחה. So neither mention is needed for the basic rule, both count as ריבויים, and the rule ריבוי אחר ריבוי למעט brings it down to half a לוג.

keyTerms.meaning: A liquid measure; the standard amount of oil for a מנחה.
At all.

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think that without ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ the תודה would have no oil. The new point is the opposite: without it, it would get a full לוג like every מנחה.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא, אִילּוּ לֹא נֶאֱמַר ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ כׇּל עִיקָּר,
phrases.english: Rather: had "with oil" not been written at all,

phrases.aramaic: הָיִיתִי אוֹמֵר הֲרֵי הוּא כְּכׇל הַמְּנָחוֹת לְלוֹג.
phrases.english: I would have said it is like all the meal offerings, with a log of oil.
Now that it says "with oil," "with oil,"
it is an amplification after an amplification,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין רִיבּוּי אַחַר רִיבּוּי אֶלָּא לְמַעֵט,
phrases.english: and an amplification after an amplification comes only to limit;
the verse limited it to half a log.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אִילּוּ לֹא נֶאֱמַר ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ כׇּל עִיקָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of Step 4 by rewording רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The first ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ is needed just to require oil.
steps.terutzMaskana: The default is already a לוג like all מנחות, so both mentions are ריבויים and they limit the amount to half a לוג.

steps.title: Should the half לוג be split equally among the three kinds of loaves?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא raises a possible idea: maybe the half לוג is divided equally among the חלות, רקיקין, and רביכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think this half לוג is divided into three kinds: for the loaves, the wafers, and the poached loaves.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and suggests a possible way to divide the oil. It is setting up the next step, which will reject this idea.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that the total is half a לוג, the question is how to share it among the three kinds of מצה in the תודה. The simple guess is three equal parts, a sixth of a לוג each.

keyTerms.meaning: You might think; it introduces an idea that will be rejected.
Loaves (here, the regular מצה loaves mixed with oil).
Thin wafers smeared with oil.
Poached loaves, made with flour scalded in hot water and oil.

phrases.aramaic: יָכוֹל יְהֵא חֲצִי לוֹג זֶה מִתְחַלֵּק לִשְׁלֹשֶׁת מִינִין,
phrases.english: You might think this half-log is divided among the three kinds:
for the loaves, for the wafers, and for the poached loaves?

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל יְהֵא חֲצִי לוֹג זֶה מִתְחַלֵּק לִשְׁלֹשֶׁת מִינִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the half לוג total and asks how it is divided.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Is the half לוג split equally among the three kinds of loaves?

steps.title: The רביכה gets half the oil
steps.stepSummary: An extra ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ by the רביכה shows it gets more oil. Half the oil goes to the רביכה, and the other half is shared by the חלות and רקיקין.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the פסוק says ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ by the רביכה, there was no need to say it, so it adds oil for the רביכה. How does it work? He brings half a לוג of oil and divides it. Half goes to the loaves and wafers, and half goes to the רביכה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא rejects the equal split. It uses an extra ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ to give the רביכה a bigger share.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil requirement was already known, so saying ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ again by the רביכה is extra. That extra word gives the רביכה more oil. The result is that the רביכה alone gets a quarter לוג, while the חלות and רקיקין share the other quarter.

keyTerms.meaning: There was no need for the verse to say it, so it must teach something extra.
It added, it increased.
How so? How does this work in practice?

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי עקיבא: the תודה gets half a לוג in total, half of that goes to the רביכה, and half is shared by the חלות and רקיקין.

phrases.english: When it says "with oil" regarding the poached loaves,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 7:12

phrases.english: which the verse had no need to say,
it added oil for the poached loaves.
How so?
He brings half a log of oil and divides it; [half of it]
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets are the corrected wording, so read it as "half of it goes to..."

phrases.english: for the loaves and the wafers, and half of it for the poached loaves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the equal split suggested in Step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רביכה gets half of the half לוג; the חלות and רקיקין share the other half.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: it is a הלכה למשה מסיני, not from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה rejects רבי עקיבא's derivation from the words ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״. He says the half לוג for תודה, along with two other rules, is a הלכה למשה מסיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said to him: עקיבא, even if you go on all day deriving from ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״ ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״, I won't listen to you. Rather, these are each a הלכה למשה מסיני: half a לוג of oil for the תודה, a רביעית of oil for a נזיר, and the eleven days between one נדה period and the next.
steps.whatsHappening: Another תנא argues with רבי עקיבא. He says the half לוג rule does not come from the פסוק at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה agrees with the amount of half a לוג. He only rejects the source. He says it is an oral law given at Sinai, and he lists it together with two other set amounts that are also הלכה למשה מסיני.

keyTerms.meaning: A law given orally to משה at Sinai, not learned from a פסוק.
A quarter of a לוג.
A nazirite; he brings loaves with oil when he finishes his נזירות.

keyTerms.term: אַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם שֶׁבֵּין נִדָּה לְנִדָּה
keyTerms.meaning: The eleven days after a נדה period; bleeding during them can make a woman a זבה.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is not arguing about the amount of oil. Both agree it is half a לוג; they only argue about where the rule comes from.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a classic argument about source: is a rule learned from the words of the פסוק, or is it an oral הלכה למשה מסיני?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: עֲקִיבָא,
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya said to him: Akiva,

phrases.aramaic: אִם אַתָּה מְרַבֶּה כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
phrases.english: even if you amplify the entire day
from "with oil," "with oil,"
I will not listen to you;
rather, half a log of oil for the thanks offering,
and a quarter-log of oil for a nazirite,

phrases.aramaic: וְאַחַד עָשָׂר יוֹם שֶׁבֵּין נִדָּה לְנִדָּה –
phrases.english: and the eleven days between one menstrual period and the next,
are a law given to Moses from Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה: עֲקִיבָא, אִם אַתָּה מְרַבֶּה כׇּל הַיּוֹם כּוּלּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source behind רבי עקיבא's derivation in Steps 5-7.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The derivation from the double ״בַּשֶּׁמֶן״, not the amount of half a לוג.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The amount is not learned from the פסוק; it is a הלכה למשה מסיני.

steps.title: Next line of the משנה: measuring with a לוג
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: one would measure the oil with a לוג measure.
steps.simpleTranslation: One would measure with a לוג.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה. It is setting up a new discussion about how the oil for the regular מנחות was measured.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This starts a new topic. After the half לוג of the תודה, the משנה turns to the standard measure of one לוג used for the oil of regular מנחות.

keyTerms.meaning: Measures.

phrases.english: With a log one would measure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the תודה discussion to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The oil for the מנחות was measured with a לוג measure.

steps.title: The Sages: every tenth of flour needs one לוג of oil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings the view of the חכמים. From the poor מצורע's פסוק, which puts 'עשרון' next to 'לוג', they learn that each עשרון of flour needs one לוג of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: about a poor מצורע it is written, 'a tenth … mixed … and a לוג'. This teaches that each tenth needs a לוג. These are the words of the חכמים.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with the first opinion about how much oil a מנחה needs: one לוג for each עשרון of flour.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The poor מצורע brings exactly one עשרון of flour together with one לוג of oil. The חכמים read this pairing as a rule for every מנחה: the oil grows with the flour, one לוג for each עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: A poor person with צרעת, who brings smaller קרבנות for his purification
A tenth of an איפה, the basic unit of flour for a מנחה
A measure of liquid, used here for the oil
Requires, needs

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
With regard to a poor leper it is written:
"A tenth … mixed … and a log"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:21. The dots stand for words of the פסוק that the ברייתא skips.

phrases.english: It teaches about a tenth that it requires a log;
these are the words of the Sages.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the משנה's line about measuring oil with a לוג measure, the גמרא brings a ברייתא on how many לוגין a מנחה needs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, each עשרון of flour in a מנחה requires one לוג of oil.

steps.title: Even a huge מנחה gets only one לוג
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר argue. Any מנחה, even one of sixty עשרונים, gets just one לוג of oil. They learn this from the words 'למנחה ולג שמן'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר say: even a מנחה of sixty tenths has only its one לוג, as it says, 'for a מנחה and a לוג of oil.'
steps.whatsHappening: The second side of the מחלוקת: the oil does not grow with the flour. Every מנחה gets one לוג, whatever its size.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They read the same פסוק differently. They pair 'לוג' with 'מנחה', not with 'עשרון'. So the rule is one לוג for each מנחה, even if it is sixty times bigger than usual.

keyTerms.meaning: A flour offering
Sixty tenths of flour, the largest מנחה a person may bring in one vessel
Its (one) לוג

phrases.english: Rabbi Nechemya and Rabbi Eliezer say:
Even a meal offering of sixty tenths
has only its one log,
as it says: "For a meal offering, and a log of oil."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:21, the same פסוק as before. Here they focus on 'מנחה' standing next to 'לוג'.

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides use the very same פסוק. The argument is only about which word the לוג is tied to: 'עשרון' (each tenth) or 'מנחה' (the whole offering).
steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר אוֹמְרִים: אֲפִילּוּ מִנְחָה שֶׁל שִׁשִּׁים עֶשְׂרוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to the חכמים in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Every מנחה requires only one לוג of oil, regardless of how much flour it has.

steps.title: How does רבי נחמיה explain the words 'a tenth … and a לוג'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב do with the phrase 'עשרון בלול ולוג', since the חכמים learned their rule from it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, what do they do with this 'a tenth, mixed, and a לוג'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the other side what that phrase teaches if not the חכמים' rule. It is setting up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק clearly ties 'עשרון' to 'לוג'. If רבי נחמיה does not learn 'one לוג per עשרון' from it, he must explain why those words are written.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? How do they use this פסוק?
Mixed (with oil)

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה וְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב,
phrases.english: And Rabbi Nechemya and Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא just said 'רבי אליעזר'. Here the גמרא gives a fuller name.

phrases.english: this "a tenth, mixed, and a log,"
what do they do with it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how the second view handles the words the first view used.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the words 'עשרון בלול ולוג' teach according to רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: The words teach that the poor מצורע brings one עשרון
steps.stepSummary: For רבי נחמיה, the phrase is needed for its plain meaning: the poor מצורע brings one עשרון. So it cannot teach a general rule about oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is needed for itself: the Torah is saying, let him bring one tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי נחמיה uses the words for their simple meaning, the amount of flour the poor מצורע brings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A פסוק is only free to teach something extra if its plain meaning is not needed. Here, says רבי נחמיה, it is needed to tell us the poor מצורע's מנחה is one עשרון. So nothing is left over for the rule 'one לוג per עשרון'.

keyTerms.meaning: For itself, for its own plain meaning
The Merciful One, meaning the Torah
Let him bring

phrases.english: That one is needed for itself,
since the Merciful One is saying:
Let him bring one tenth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase teaches its plain meaning: the poor מצורע brings one עשרון of flour. So it cannot also teach how much oil goes with each עשרון.

steps.title: The Sages: the one עשרון is already obvious
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים answer that the plain meaning is not needed. The rich מצורע brings three קרבנות and three עשרונים, so the poor one, with one קרבן, obviously brings one עשרון. That frees the words to teach 'one לוג per עשרון'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side says it is not needed for itself. The Torah showed that the מצורע brings three קרבנות and three tenths. So here, with one קרבן, it is one tenth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the חכמים' reply: we already know the poor מצורע brings one עשרון, so the words are extra and teach the oil rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rich מצורע's three animals go with three עשרונים, one עשרון per קרבן. The poor מצורע brings one animal, so we would already know he brings one עשרון. Since the plain meaning is already known, the words 'עשרון … ולוג' are free to teach that each עשרון needs a לוג.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (here, the חכמים)
Revealed, showed clearly
Animal offerings
Here (in the case of the poor מצורע)

phrases.english: And the other side: it is not needed for itself,
since the Merciful One revealed about a leper
phrases.notes: This is the regular, not-poor מצורע.

phrases.english: three offerings and three tenths,
here, where there is one offering, one tenth.

steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a פסוק teaches something extra only if its plain meaning is not needed. They argue about whether 'one עשרון for the poor מצורע' is already known from the rich מצורע. The חכמים say yes, so they get 'one לוג per עשרון'. רבי נחמיה says no, so he holds one לוג per מנחה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This decides whether a large מנחה needs many לוגין of oil or just one.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The חכמים answer step 13's claim that the phrase is needed for its plain meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the plain meaning is already known from another source, so the words are extra.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'עשרון בלול ולוג' are needed to tell us the poor מצורע brings one עשרון, so they cannot teach the oil rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The one עשרון is known from the rich מצורע's pattern of one עשרון per קרבן. So the words are extra and teach that each עשרון needs a לוג.

steps.title: Why רבי נחמיה still needs the plain meaning
steps.stepSummary: רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב explain why the פסוק had to state that the poor מצורע brings an עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: The other side says the words were needed. You might have thought that since the Torah had pity on the poor מצורע and let him bring a cheap offering, he does not need to bring a מנחה at all.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נחמיה's side answers the חכמים' claim from step 14. The חכמים said the plain meaning was obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים argued that the poor מצורע's one עשרון is obvious. רבי נחמיה says it is not obvious. Since the Torah already made things easier for the poor man, we might have thought it removed the מנחה from him completely. So the words are needed to teach that he still brings an עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have thought (the starting assumption the גמרא sets up in order to reject it)
The Torah (the Merciful One) had pity
Poverty: the cheaper offering of a poor person

phrases.english: And the other: it was needed,
phrases.notes: 'The other' here means רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

phrases.english: it would enter your mind to say:
since the Merciful One had pity on him
to let him bring an offering of poverty,
say he does not need a meal offering at all.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets, מנה; the word in square brackets, מנחה, is the corrected wording.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rebuts step 14's claim that the plain meaning is obvious.
steps.terutzResolutionType: איצטריך: shows the verse is needed against a mistaken assumption
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A poor מצורע might be fully exempt from a מנחה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The verse is needed to teach that he brings one עשרון, so it cannot also teach the oil rule.

steps.title: The חכמים: the Torah never fully exempts a poor person
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים reply that we never find the Torah exempting a poor person completely. So the mistaken idea would never come up.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side says: we never find that a poor person is completely exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים push back against רבי נחמיה's reason from step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah makes things cheaper for a poor person, but it never cancels his obligation completely. So nobody would think the poor מצורע brings no מנחה. The words are still free to teach 'one לוג per עשרון'.

keyTerms.meaning: Completely, entirely
We have not found (there is no example of this)

phrases.english: And the other:
phrases.notes: Now 'the other' is the חכמים.

phrases.english: completely [exempt], we have not found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the הוה אמינא proposed in step 15.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Denies the premise of the opposing hava amina
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A poor person might be fully exempt.
steps.terutzMaskana: Poverty only lowers an obligation and never removes it, so the plain meaning is obvious and the words teach the oil rule.
steps.whatToRemember: The חכמים learn 'one לוג per עשרון' from the poor מצורע's פסוק. רבי נחמיה needs that פסוק to teach that the poor man still brings an עשרון.

steps.title: What do the חכמים do with 'למנחה ולג שמן'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how the חכמים use the words that רבי נחמיה learned his rule from.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים: what do they do with this phrase, 'for a meal offering and a לוג of oil'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now turns the question around, as it did in step 12. Now it asks the חכמים to explain רבי נחמיה's source words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 11, רבי נחמיה learned 'one לוג for any מנחה' from 'למנחה ולג שמן'. The חכמים do not accept that rule, so they must use these words for something else.

keyTerms.meaning: What do they do with it? (How do they use this verse?)

phrases.english: And the Rabbis,
this: "for a meal offering and a log of oil"
what do they do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבָּנַן, הַאי לְמִנְחָה וְלֹג שֶׁמֶן מַאי עָבְדִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror of step 12: now the חכמים must explain the opposing source.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the חכמים learn from 'למנחה ולג שמן'.

steps.title: A donated מנחה must be at least an עשרון
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים use the phrase to teach that someone who donates a מנחה cannot bring less than an amount that takes one לוג of oil, which is an עשרון.
steps.simpleTranslation: That phrase is about someone who donates a מנחה. He may not bring less than an amount that needs one לוג of oil. What is that amount? An עשרון.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 17. It gives the חכמים a different lesson from these words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'מנחה' and 'לוג' are placed together. The חכמים read this as a minimum size: a מנחה must be big enough to need one לוג. By their own rule, one לוג goes with one עשרון, so the minimum is an עשרון.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who donates a voluntary offering
That he should not bring less than
A tenth of an איפה, the basic measure of flour for a מנחה

phrases.english: That is for one who donates a meal offering,
that he should not bring less than an amount that requires a log,
and what is that? A tenth of an ephah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 17.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The words teach the minimum size of a donated מנחה: one עשרון.

steps.title: רבי נחמיה learns both lessons from the same words
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where רבי נחמיה learns the minimum-size rule. It answers that he learns two things from the same phrase.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other side? You learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question and answers it. רבי נחמיה gets both the minimum-size rule and the 'one לוג for any מנחה' rule from 'למנחה ולג שמן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think רבי נחמיה has no source for the minimum-size rule, since he used the phrase for his oil rule. The answer is that the phrase can carry both lessons at once.

keyTerms.meaning: You can learn two things from it

phrases.english: And the other?
phrases.notes: The question is left out but assumed: where do רבי נחמיה and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב learn the minimum size?

phrases.english: Learn two things from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the source discussion by showing רבי נחמיה also has the minimum-size rule.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: One phrase teaches both the minimum size and the one-לוג rule.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a donated מנחה is at least an עשרון. They argue about how much oil a large מנחה needs.

steps.title: Where do six, four, and three לוגין come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's amounts for the נסכים of a פר, איל, and כבש, and asks for their source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Six for a bull, four for a ram, three for a lamb. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. It sets up a question about the amounts of oil and wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These numbers are in לוגין. The גמרא wants a פסוק behind them, which it brings in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: A bull
A ram
A lamb

phrases.english: Six for a bull,

steps.title: The פסוק: half, a third, and a quarter of a הין
steps.stepSummary: The source is the פסוק that gives the נסכים as half a הין for a פר, with smaller fractions for an איל and a כבש.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And their נסכים shall be half a הין for the bull.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 20 with a פסוק that measures the נסכים in parts of a הין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק gives fractions of a הין: half, a third, a quarter. It does not give לוגין. To turn these into 6, 4, and 3, we still need to know how many לוגין are in a הין. The next step supplies that.

keyTerms.meaning: The wine poured on the מזבח with a קרבן
A measure of liquid

phrases.english: As it is written:
"And their libations shall be half a hin for the bull."
phrases.notes: במדבר 28:14. The פסוק goes on: a third of a הין for the ram and a quarter for the lamb.

steps.triggerLanguage: דִּכְתִיב: וְנִסְכֵּיהֶם חֲצִי הַהִין יִהְיֶה לַפָּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 20.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק gives ½, ⅓, and ¼ of a הין.

steps.title: A הין is twelve לוגין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves that a הין equals twelve לוגין from the word 'זה' in the פסוק about the anointing oil. The גימטריא of 'זה' is twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: A הין is twelve לוגין. It is written 'olive oil, a הין', and it is written 'holy anointing oil, this shall be to Me for your generations'. 'זה' (this) has the number value twelve.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fills in the missing piece. It shows how many לוגין are in a הין, so the fractions in the פסוק turn into 6, 4, and 3.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The anointing oil was one הין. The פסוק calls it 'זה'. ז is 7 and ה is 5, so 'זה' adds up to 12. That hints that the הין was twelve לוגין. Half of 12 is 6, a third is 4, and a quarter is 3, which matches the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: A smaller liquid measure; twelve make a הין
The holy anointing oil made by משה
The number value of Hebrew letters

this shall be to Me for your generations",

phrases.notes: ז is 7 and ה is 5, which together make 12.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: One הין equals twelve לוגין, learned from the גימטריא of 'זה'.
steps.whatToRemember: A הין is 12 לוגין. So a פר gets ½ (6), an איל ⅓ (4), and a כבש ¼ (3).

steps.title: Where do we learn half a log of oil for each lamp?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's amount for the מנורה and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Three and a half לוג go to the מנורה, half a לוג for each lamp. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the last oil amount in the משנה, the oil for the מנורה, and asks where it comes from. This sets up the next step, which gives the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The מנורה has seven lamps, and seven times half a לוג is three and a half לוג. So the real question is where the half-לוג per lamp comes from. This follows the same pattern as the earlier questions about the נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden lamp with seven lamps in the בית המקדש
A single lamp of the מנורה

steps.title: The oil must last from evening until morning
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads 'מערב עד בקר' to mean each lamp must get enough oil to burn the whole night.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: 'From evening to morning' means give the lamp its full amount, so that it keeps burning from evening until morning.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא. The פסוק says the מנורה burns 'from evening to morning', so each lamp must get enough oil to last all night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק does not give a number. It only sets a goal: the oil must last the whole night. The actual amount comes in step 26.

steps.title: A second lesson from 'from evening to morning'
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא gives another reading: lighting the מנורה is the only עבודה that is valid all through the night.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another explanation of 'From evening to morning': there is no other עבודה that is valid from evening until morning except this one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives a second lesson from the same words. The מנורה is the only עבודה that may be done at any time through the night.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This 'דבר אחר' reads the words as a rule about time, not about the amount of oil. Other עבודות are done in the daytime, but the מנורה's work belongs to the whole night.

steps.title: The חכמים measured half a log for the whole night
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים worked out that half a לוג is the amount that lasts from evening until morning.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים measured that half a לוג lasts from evening until morning.
steps.whatsHappening: This line finishes the answer to step 23. The פסוק requires enough oil for the whole night, and the חכמים measured that this is half a לוג.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק sets the goal, and the measurement fills in the number. So the half-לוג per lamp is based on a test, not on a word of the פסוק.

steps.title: Two opinions on how the חכמים did the measuring
steps.stepSummary: One opinion says they began with more oil and cut back. The other says they began with less and added.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say they measured from above to below, and some say they measured from below to above.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings two opinions on how the חכמים tested the amount of oil. This sets up the next step, which explains the reason for each one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'From above to below' means starting with more oil than needed and using less each night until it ran out just at morning. 'From below to above' means starting with too little and adding each night until it lasted all night.

steps.title: The reason behind each way of measuring
steps.stepSummary: Adding up protects the money of כלל ישראל. Cutting down fits the rule that there is no poverty in a place of wealth.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who says they measured from below to above holds that the Torah cares about the money of ישראל. The one who says they measured from above to below holds that there is no poverty in a place of wealth.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why each opinion chose its way of measuring.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Starting small wastes less oil, because the Torah is careful with the money of ישראל. Starting big uses a lot of oil, but in the בית המקדש we do not act cheaply, since it is a place of wealth.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Adding up saves money for ישראל. Cutting down reflects that the בית המקדש is never run cheaply.
steps.whyThisMatters: Both reasons are general rules that come up in other places in the גמרא about spending on מצוות and on the בית המקדש.

steps.title: New משנה: which נסכים may be mixed together
steps.stepSummary: The משנה allows mixing the נסכים of bulls with those of rams, lambs with lambs, and an individual's with the community's.
steps.simpleTranslation: We may mix the נסכים of bulls with the נסכים of rams, the נסכים of lambs with the נסכים of lambs, and those of an individual with those of the community.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists which נסכים may be mixed together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נסכים of a bull and of a ram use the same amount of oil for each עשרון of flour, so they may be mixed. The נסכים of a lamb use a different amount of oil, so they are only mixed with other lambs' נסכים.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (marks the start of a new משנה)
We may mix together
The נסכים (flour, oil and wine brought with an animal קרבן)
An individual
The community

steps.confusionAlert: 'Lambs with lambs' does not mean lambs are a special case. Lambs' נסכים simply have a different amount of oil, so they cannot be mixed with those of bulls or rams.
